$comment: Default factory settings. A target repo overrides any subset in its own .factory.json at the repo root; unset keys fall back to these. See global/factory/readme.md for what each knob does and docs/factory-playbook.md for how to tune them.
$comment_cli: Version of @anthropic-ai/claude-code the worker installs. 'latest' tracks upstream; pin an exact version (e.g. '2.1.272') if you want an unattended run to be reproducible and to choose when it moves.
$comment_runner: require_self_hosted fails a factory job that lands on a GitHub-hosted runner. Turn it on when the factory must run on your own hardware -- on a Claude subscription via CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, and without spending Actions minutes. The runner labels themselves come from the FACTORY_RUNNER repository variable, since `runs-on` is evaluated before any step can read this file.
$comment_host: Host capacity guard. wip_limit counts FACTORY work; a self-hosted box shares itself with CI, a Docker swarm, and everything else on it. These thresholds are asked of the machine, so a busy host defers rather than piling on. A deferred run releases its claim and requeues -- nothing consumed, nothing escalated. Linux-only (/proc); reports ok elsewhere rather than guessing.
$comment_queue: hold_labels match case-insensitively; an entry ending in * matches by prefix. Use the prefix form when the repo has a SECOND automation keyed on a label family (e.g. "agent*" where another pipeline triggers on any agent:* label) -- admitting such an issue would put two agents on one issue and race them to open competing pull requests.
$comment_audits: Each audit takes an optional one-line `notes` string, threaded into the auditor's prompt as repo-specific scope. Use it to say what this repo has already decided -- e.g. that certain docs are knowingly stale and only NEW drift is worth filing -- so the audit does not re-file an accepted decision every cycle, which is how this feature gets switched off.
